Title: Their Lonely Betters
Content: As I listened from a beach-chair in the shade
To all the noises that my garden made,
It seemed to me only proper that words
Should be withheld from vegetables and birds.
A robin with no Christian name ran through
The Robin-Anthem which was all it knew,
And rustling flowers for some `text(third)` party waited
To say which pairs, if any, should get mated.
Not `text(one)` of them was capable of lying,
There was not `text(one)` which knew that it was dying
Or could have with a rhythm or a rhyme
Let them leave language to their lonely betters
Who count some `text(days)` and long for certain letters;
We, too, make noises when we laugh or weep:
Words are for those with promises to keep.
